question.text: A clearing member discovers that one of its trading members has defaulted on margin obligations. What is the standard procedure?

answer.text: The clearing member must meet the trading member's obligations and, if the clearing member itself defaults, the clearing corporation's default waterfall is invoked
The clearing corporation immediately halts all trading on the exchange
Other trading members share the loss equally
The clearing member has no responsibility for the trading member's default

explanation.text: The Logic: Clearing members are responsible for the obligations of the trading members they clear. To meet the shortfall, margin may be blocked sequentially from client collateral, then trading member proprietary collateral, then clearing member proprietary collateral. If the defaulting party is the clearing member or another defaulting member, the workbook sets out a default waterfall starting with the monies of the defaulting member (including its Core SGF contribution), then insurance, then clearing corporation resources, then Core SGF components, then remaining clearing corporation and stock exchange resources, then a capped additional contribution by non-defaulting members, and finally a payout haircut. The Trap: Trading does not halt for one member's default. Losses are absorbed through the prescribed waterfall, not divided equally among all members. The clearing member is not insulated from its trading member's obligations. Note: Distinguish a trading member default (cleared by its CM) from a CM or defaulting-member default (which triggers the full clearing corporation waterfall on page 273 of the workbook).
